To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) neonatal exposure to estradiol improves acquisition of a spatial task in male and female rats; (2) the effect of estradiol is specific for spatial tasks, since the effect is observed only when spatial information is available and not when the information is nonspatial; (3) the effect of neonatal exposure to estrogen is not due to a direct effect of estrogen on the hippocampus but rather is a consequence of organizational effects of early estrogen exposure on the brain; and

(1) neonatally castrating rats (MNC) or neonatally treating female rats with estradiol (FNE) results in impaired spatial memory; (2) neonatally treating male rats with estradiols (MNE) results in improved performance in a radial maze; (3) the effect of neonatal gonadal steroids on spatial memory is due to organizational effects of early exposure to gonadotropins; (4) the effect of gonadal steroids

neonatally castrating male rats and treating female rats neonatally with estrogen benzoate disrupts the development of spatial memory in a way that suggests that the organizational action of early gonadal hormones is to improve the acquisition of spatial memory by simplifying the perceptual processes that guide the ability to remember the spatial layout of the environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of early gonadally mediated events on the development of spatial memory in rats.
the role of early hormonal exposure on the development of spatial memory.
the role of gonadal secretions in early life on later sexual differentiation of spatial memory in male and female rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
early exposure to estradiol in males and early castration in females may have a beneficial effect on spatial memory, but the mechanism is not clear.
the organizational effect of estradiol on spatial memory is mediated by its action on the hippocampus.
the organizational effects of early gonad secretions are not only limited to sexual behavior but also extend to other behaviors that are sensitive to the organizational effects of gonadal secretions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neonatal exposure to estradiol facilitates spatial learning and memory.
the early exposure to gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) is a critical event in the development of the brain.
early gonadal secretory products have a significant effect on the way in which the brain processes spatial information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
early exposure to sex hormones may influence spatial memory in adulthood.
the early exposure to gonad hormones (probably estradiols) improves the acquisition of spatial tasks.
the early exposure to gonads hormones (probably estradiols) improve acquisition of spatial tasks.
